lessons.statement: Every rendered claim string on any surface (student, board, AND teacher director/mirror) must be a computed, audited atom from the first commit of a module — hand-written claim copy was the single largest defect class across all three M2 lessons (pooled curves, false attributions, wrong nouns, wrong magnitudes, wrong-arm scripts), and every instance was eliminated only once claims were structurally bound and swept (value/quantifier/bound/noun/level plus rendered-string drift, mutation-proven).

A verification instrument is not done until it is proven non-vacuous by mutation: geometry-only fold assertions missed z-index occlusion, atom-only audits missed rendered-string drift, a dominance limb was tautological, and a fit guard missed ink overprint — in each case the repaired instrument was accepted only after a seeded defect demonstrably failed it.

A blocking dissent may be resolved only on the owning critic's explicit discharge line in their own gate artifact — the one resolution closed on an instrument exit code alone was caught by the analyst as a provenance violation and had to be re-adjudicated.

Critic role activations and completions must be ledgered under the critic role's own actor identity, not the lead's — lead-actor bookkeeping made genuinely independent reviews read as self-certification at the wave gate.

In a design war, at least one candidate should be produced genuinely clean-room (prior implementation and its analyses redacted from context): the sunk-cost-blind candidate won the M2 architecture war on all three independent rankings.

A Level-3 quality war over a three-lesson flagship consumed roughly four times the soft agent budget of 14 (build + gate + repair + re-adjudication cycles across six review functions); the routing prior for flagship module wars should budget accordingly rather than treat the overrun as an anomaly.
